items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: his friend Lenny Russo was a drummer who I worked with

ctx.x: Do you have a sense — I’m going to refer back to that “Nature Boy” recording because there’s some pretty sophisticated orchestrations behind you. Do you have the kind of ear and chordal knowledge that you know what those chords are when you’re improvising over them?

Yes I do. I do. And I learned that — I was born with perfect pitch so I hear all the inner voices and everything that’s going on, I hear them all. So when I first started playing jazz I was, well I was probably twelve. And my brother was — my brother was also a piano © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

player and very nice, and he would come over to the house, I mean he’d be at the house and his friend Lenny Russo was a drummer who I worked with and I used to sit in the back seat with his drums on these gigs when I was fourteen but he’d be there and they’d play the blues. I’ll never forget it. They’d start playing the blues, B flat blues, and my brother says to me, “Play.” I said, “Play what?” He said, “Just play.” So I started playing and when it would go to the four chord if I hit the wrong note on the four…
